newsitem.title: FRANCE: Parents of dead French boy want Zaire envoy charged.
newsitem.headline: Parents of dead French boy want Zaire envoy charged.

text.p: The parents of a French teenager killed when hit by a car driven by Zaire's ambassador to France called on Zairean authorities on Wednesday to waive his diplomatic immunity to allow him to face possible charges.

The parents of Raphael Lenoir, 13, said they sent a message asking Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko to waive ambassador Ramazani Baya's diplomatic immunity, which is possible under the Vienna convention governing such matters.
Another boy, aged 12, was seriously injured when they were hit by the vehicle, a hired car which Baya was driving along the seafront in Menton on the French Riviera on Saturday.
Police said Baya's car apparently swerved off the road before hitting the two boys. The 12-year-old was in a coma in Nice hospital.
Baya had travelled to Menton to visit Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko, convalescing in Roquebrune Cap Martin on the Riviera after cancer surgery in August.
Police said Baya had undergone a breathalyser test which showed that he was over the limit. But then the envoy claimed diplomatic immunity protecting him from legal pursuit.
